clinician.trajectory_summary: An 87-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, and prior lung cancer, presented with anorexia, nausea, and acute kidney injury (serum creatinine 428 μmol/L from a baseline of 187 μmol/L). Initial workup revealed a right lower ureter mass with hydronephrosis. Biopsy of the ureteral orifice bulge showed fibrous tissue with IgG-positive and IgG4-positive plasma cells. A kidney biopsy confirmed diabetic nephropathy and IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis (IgG4-TIN), characterized by abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells and storiform fibrosis. Serum IgG4 was significantly elevated (1890 mg/dL). A double-J stent was placed, which led to a decrease in serum creatinine. The patient was then treated with methylprednisolone, resulting in further improvement of serum creatinine to 196 μmol/L and a decrease in serum IgG4 to 171 mg/dL after two months.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute kidney injury (AKI) on chronic kidney disease (CKD).
CT revealed a right lower ureter mass with right renal and ureter hydronephrosis.
Biopsy of the right ureteral orifice bulge showed extruded and deformed fibrous tissue with small IgG-positive and IgG4-positive plasma cells, suggesting IgG4-related ureteral involvement.
Renal biopsy confirmed diabetic nephropathy, characterized by mesangial cell and matrix proliferation, diffuse homogeneous thickening of the basement membrane, and diffuse fusion of foot processes.

Renal biopsy confirmed IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis (IgG4-TIN), evidenced by abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells in the renal interstitial (more than 25 per high power field), IgG4+:IgG ratio > 35%, and storiform pattern fibrosis.
Serum IgG4 was significantly increased (1890 mg/dL), supporting the diagnosis of IgG4-related disease.
Placement of a double-J stent in the right ureter led to an initial decrease in serum creatinine, indicating relief of ureteral obstruction.

Treatment with methylprednisolone resulted in significant improvement in serum creatinine (from 428 μmol/L to 196 μmol/L) and serum IgG4 (from 1890 mg/dL to 171 mg/dL) after two months, confirming the responsiveness of IgG4-related disease to corticosteroids.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Malignancy as the sole cause of ureteral obstruction
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Urine cytology was negative (E000), and ureteral biopsy showed fibrous tissue with IgG4-positive plasma cells (E005) rather than malignant cells. The response to steroids also makes malignancy less likely as the primary cause of obstruction.
